title: Allu Arjun Is Summoned to Court Over the Pushpa 2 Stampede. The Man Who Plays the Untouchable Hero Must Now Stand Before a Judge.
excerpt: Eighteen months after a fan died in the crush at a Pushpa 2 premiere, Hyderabad's Nampally Court has ordered the superstar to appear in person on June 22.
body:
On December 4, 2024, the lobby of Hyderabad's Sandhya Theatre was supposed to be a coronation. **Pushpa 2: The Rule** was opening worldwide, **Allu Arjun** — the biggest male star Telugu cinema has ever produced — was arriving in person, and thousands of fans had packed RTC Cross Roads to catch a glimpse of him. By the end of the night, a 35-year-old woman named Revathi was dead of suffocation in the crush, and her young son Sri Teja lay in a hospital bed with severe head injuries. The premiere of the most-watched Indian film of its year had turned into a tragedy.

Eighteen months later, that night is back in the headlines — and this time the marquee name is in the dock. On June 19, the **Nampally Court** in Hyderabad summoned Allu Arjun to appear in person on Monday, June 22, as the criminal case over the Sandhya stampede finally moves toward trial.

> "Nampally Court has issued summons to actor Allu Arjun to appear in person before the court on Monday for a hearing. We will give more details later about the matter." — Allu Arjun's legal team

It is a stark line for a star who, in the *Pushpa* films, plays a man the system cannot touch. In the real proceedings, **Chikkadpally Police** have named the actor as Accused No. 11. The management of Sandhya Theatre is listed as Accused Nos. 1 to 10 — the venue blamed first, the star tagged behind them. Reports say the court has issued summons to 19 of the accused, and that police have already filed a chargesheet against 23 people in all. The hearing on Monday is procedural, the start of a trial that will examine crowd-control arrangements, the coordination — or lack of it — between the actor's team, the theatre and the police, and the circumstances that let a celebration become fatal.

The legal backbone of the case sits in the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita**, the penal code that replaced the old IPC, under provisions covering negligence. Police have maintained that neither the actor's team nor the theatre informed them in advance of the visit, leaving the venue without adequate crowd management on a night when thousands were always going to turn up for a glimpse of Pushpa himself.

This is not the first time the case has touched Allu Arjun directly. On December 13, 2024 — nine days after the stampede — the actor was arrested by Hyderabad City Police, only for the **Telangana High Court** to grant him interim bail the same day. He has since called Revathi's death a source of deep grief and pledged financial help to her family. His wife, **Sneha Reddy**, reportedly visited Sri Teja's family, assuring them the family would cover the educational expenses of his younger sister; the actor's camp and the *Pushpa* production team are said to have funded the boy's medical treatment as he undergoes long-term rehabilitation for catastrophic injuries.

None of that pauses the trial, and that is precisely the point. India has watched the gap between a star's box-office invincibility and a courtroom's indifference to it widen for years, and this case lands squarely in that fault line. The same fan frenzy that turns a *Pushpa* opening into a record-shattering event is the frenzy that killed someone outside the theatre — and the law is now asking who bears responsibility when adulation tips into a crush.

For the diaspora, the *Pushpa* franchise has been one of the great crossover stories of the decade — Allu Arjun's "thaggede le" swagger lighting up theatres from New Jersey to Sydney, the films routinely among the highest-grossing Indian releases on the overseas circuit. Monday's hearing is a reminder that the spectacle has a cost ledger most fans never see, and that the management of crowds at premieres — long treated as a logistics afterthought — is now a matter for the courts.

Allu Arjun, meanwhile, has work waiting on the other side of the case. He is attached to **Raaka** (also reported as *Raaka*/*Raaku*), the dark fantasy spectacle that will be his next big swing, and the *Pushpa* universe itself remains the most valuable property in his career. Whether he appears in person on June 22 or sends a legal request to be excused, the image will carry: the superstar who plays the man above the law, standing inside a courtroom that intends to test exactly that idea.

The trial will be slow, technical and unglamorous — a long way from the red dust and the whistles of a *Pushpa* mass scene. But it is the most consequential frame Allu Arjun will stand in this year, and the verdict, whenever it comes, will say something about whether stardom in India still buys a pass it can no longer afford.
